1.visual: The Bluetooth symbol — a stylized angular rune resembling a capital B fused with a vertical line through it.
1.usage: Bluetooth device pairing, wireless peripheral settings, audio output selector, device connection panel

2.visual: The Bluetooth symbol with a diagonal slash crossing through it, indicating the feature is off or unavailable.
2.usage: Bluetooth disabled state, wireless toggle in off position, no Bluetooth connection indicator, airplane mode detail

3.visual: A monitor or TV screen outline with a small wireless signal arc and dot in its bottom-left corner, representing casting.
3.usage: Cast to screen, screen mirroring, Chromecast or AirPlay button, wireless display connection

4.visual: A cloud outline with a diagonal slash through it, indicating cloud access is blocked or unavailable.
4.usage: Cloud sync disabled, offline mode indicator, no cloud storage access, cloud error state

5.visual: A cloud shape with two circular refresh arrows overlaid on it, indicating cloud sync or data refresh in progress.
5.usage: Cloud sync in progress, backup syncing, cloud data refresh, file upload/download cycle

6.visual: A globe divided by a horizontal equator and vertical meridian with curved longitude arcs, representing the internet.
6.usage: Website or internet link, language and region selector, global settings, public network indicator

7.visual: A hierarchical tree with one square node at top connected by lines to two square child nodes below it.
7.usage: Org chart, network topology, site hierarchy, parent-child relationship map

8.visual: An electrical plug viewed head-on with two downward-pointing prongs and a short handle at the top.
8.usage: Power connection, plugin or integration, connect to service, charging or power status

9.visual: A broadcast tower mast with three curved signal arcs radiating outward on both left and right sides.
9.usage: Cellular tower, radio broadcast, signal transmission, wireless network coverage map

10.visual: A rectangular router box with two small dots on its face and wireless signal arcs rising from the top.
10.usage: Wi-Fi router settings, home network configuration, modem status, internet hardware management

11.visual: A small filled dot at lower-left with two progressively larger curved arcs sweeping upward and right — the RSS feed symbol.
11.usage: RSS feed subscription, blog or news feed, content updates, podcast feed link

12.visual: Four vertical bars of increasing height from left to right, representing graduated signal or reception strength.
12.usage: Cellular signal strength, network reception quality, connection quality indicator, mobile signal meter

13.visual: Two electrical plug connectors facing each other diagonally and slightly separated, suggesting a disconnected link.
13.usage: Disconnected integration, broken API connection, unplug action, connection failure status

14.visual: Full Wi-Fi symbol — a dot at the bottom with three progressively larger concentric arcs above it, indicating strong signal.
14.usage: Strong Wi-Fi signal, connected to wireless network, full wireless strength, network status indicator

15.visual: Partial Wi-Fi symbol — a dot at the bottom with two concentric arcs above it, indicating medium signal strength.
15.usage: Medium Wi-Fi signal, moderate wireless strength, fair connection quality, network signal indicator

16.visual: Minimal Wi-Fi symbol — a dot at the bottom with only one small arc above it, indicating a weak signal.
16.usage: Weak Wi-Fi signal, low wireless strength, poor connection warning, minimum signal indicator

17.visual: A Wi-Fi symbol with a diagonal slash across it, indicating no wireless network connection.
17.usage: Wi-Fi disabled, no network connection, disconnected wireless state, Wi-Fi turned off indicator

18.visual: A single small filled dot with no arcs or other elements, representing zero signal or a fully disconnected state.
18.usage: No signal state, offline indicator, zero connectivity, baseline dot for signal icon with no active arcs
